seo.metaTitle: Set PNG Alpha Channel - Uniform Opacity, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Give every pixel of a PNG the same opacity, or restore full opacity to a faded image. One percentage, colors untouched. Free, runs in your browser.
seo.longDescription: Setting the alpha channel writes one and the same opacity into every pixel of the image, while the colors stay untouched. That is different from scaling the existing transparency: a logo that is already half transparent at the edges becomes uniformly 50 percent everywhere after this operation, and a picture someone flattened to a single low opacity can be brought back to solid. It is the fastest way to make a whole PNG translucent, or to repair an image whose alpha channel was flattened. The file is processed in your browser and never uploaded.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set the percentage: 100 makes every pixel fully opaque, 50 makes them all half transparent.
Check the preview - the checkerboard shows how much transparency is left.
Save the result as PNG or WebP from the Download button to keep the alpha channel.

faq.q: How is this different from changing image opacity?
faq.a: Changing opacity multiplies the existing alpha, so the differences between more and less transparent pixels are preserved. Setting the alpha channel overwrites it: every pixel ends up with exactly the same value. Use multiply when you want to keep the picture's own transparency, and overwrite when you need it uniform.

faq.q: Can this restore a faded PNG?
faq.a: Yes, if the image still has an alpha channel and only the values are low: set 100 percent and every pixel becomes fully opaque again. If transparency was already flattened into a solid background color, no alpha channel is left to restore - the pixels are just background-colored.
No. Only the alpha value is written; the red, green and blue channels are copied byte for byte.
